q: All living organisms are composed of basic functional units called cells.
e: This statement is true because cells are recognized as the fundamental building blocks of all living organisms.

q: The simplest organisms are made up of multiple cells which perform all the functions of life.
e: The correct fact is that the simplest organisms are made up of single cells.

q: Cells are specialized to carry out particular functions in plants or animals.
e: This is true as different types of cells have specific roles that contribute to the overall functioning of the organism.

q: Complex organisms are composed of thousands of cells.
e: The correct fact is that complex organisms are composed of millions of cells.

q: Cells contain a blueprint outlining their growth, development, and function.
e: This statement is true as cells have genetic material that provides instructions for their activities.

q: All cells are derived from other cells by means of division.
e: This is a fundamental principle of cell theory, indicating that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

q: Cells are the largest units of living things.
e: The correct fact is that cells are the smallest units of living things.

q: Within cells, chemical reactions of life occur in sites and structures known as organelles.
e: This statement is true because organelles are specialized structures within cells that facilitate various biochemical processes.

q: Plant and animal cells have common features which include a plasma membrane, a nucleus and cytoplasm.
e: This statement is true as both plant and animal cells share these fundamental components essential for their function.

q: Not all ultrastructures of a cell are seen with a light microscope.
e: This is true because some organelles are too small to be resolved by a light microscope.

q: Cells of different organisms are identical in terms of shape, size, and internal organization.
e: The correct fact is that cells of different organisms are diverse in terms of shape, size, and internal organization.

q: The diversity in cell shape and structure reflects the different functions of cells.
e: This statement is true as the form of a cell is closely related to its specific function.

q: Animal tissues can be classified into three basic groups: epithelial, connective, and muscle.
e: The correct fact is that animal tissues can be classified into four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous.

q: The cytoplasm is a jelly-like structure in which organelles are embedded.
e: This statement is true as the cytoplasm provides a medium for organelles to function and interact.

q: The cell wall is present in all animal cells.
e: The correct fact is that the cell wall is absent in animal cells.

q: Ribosomes are tiny organelles that make proteins according to instructions from the genes.
e: This statement is true because ribosomes play a crucial role in protein synthesis.

q: Cells are organized into tissues, organs, and organ systems.
e: This statement is true as it describes the hierarchical organization of biological systems.

q: In multicellular organisms, all cells perform the same functions independently.
e: The correct fact is that in multicellular organisms, cells often have specialized functions and work together.

q: A tissue is a group of cells with similar structures working together to perform a particular function.
e: This statement is true as it defines what a tissue is in biological terms.

q: Organs are composed of a single type of tissue only.
e: The correct fact is that organs are composed of multiple types of tissues working together.

q: The root system in plants is composed of main roots and branches.
e: This statement is true as the root system serves to absorb water and minerals from the soil.

q: Animal tissues consist of five basic groups.
e: The correct fact is that animal tissues consist of four basic groups: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous.

q: The seven main systems in the human body include the digestive system, gas exchange system, and circulatory system.
e: This statement is true as these are indeed part of the major systems in the human body.

q: The heart is an example of an organ that contains only muscle tissue.
e: The correct fact is that the heart contains cardiac muscle, connective tissue, and epithelial tissue.
